notes.note: Stopping of remaining PTCs is only observed indirectly: the PTC would set fail after 10 s; the MTC ends immediately and execute has a 5 s timeout, so pass means the test case ended without waiting for the PTC. The test cannot observe the PTC state after the test case has ended.
Infinite queue size cannot be tested; the test checks FIFO order of 100 queued messages.
Broader reading chosen: both a message and a procedure call (nowait) are queued and stay stored until the MTC processes them after a delay.

Reading 'component A itself' chosen (two connects of mtc:p1 to other MTC ports). Verdict ttcn3verdict:error because restriction 9.1 b) requires runtime checks to cause a test case error; a tool that rejects at compile-time is also conforming in spirit. The same applies to 9.1-014a, 015a, 016a, 019a, 019b.
Component-side reading chosen: one component port mapped to two system ports.
Uses connect(system:..., system:...), which is statically detectable (21.1.1 b) 2)), hence a reject test.

Reading 'checks not possible at compile-time are made at runtime' chosen: the second connect target is selected via a function with a rnd()-based argument, so the violation is only detectable at runtime; expected verdict error.
Implicit-or-explicit reading chosen; the test uses an explicit system clause. The implicit case is covered by 9.2-023a/024a.
'Generally' read as guideline, so only a positive test (test case with MTC, PTC and system clause) is written; omission is not tested as an error.
Titan warning wrong: clause 10 says TTCN-3 constants are runtime constants, so a local constant may be initialized from a component variable; Titan only supports static constant initializers.
Tested as a constant declaration without value at the place of declaration (reject).
Reading 'identifier declared only once within its scope' chosen: duplicate module-level constant definition is rejected.
Titan warning wrong: Titan does not implement automatic typing (clause 6.5), 'const c_implicit := 2;' is valid V4.17.1 syntax.
Titan warning wrong: Titan does not implement automatic typing (clause 6.5).
Titan rejects this reject test only because it lacks automatic typing, not because of the type mismatch.
First reading chosen: optional fields of record/set constants and of a record field nested in a constant.
General reading chosen (any address value); the null address is passed as a parameter so the error is a runtime error (ttcn3verdict:error).
Treated as a runtime error (the constant is initialized from an unbound component variable), hence ttcn3verdict:error. Titan warning is due to its lack of runtime constants, not to this rule.
